assessment_summary: The statement claims that in any tree on 2 to 7 vertices, every vertex of degree at least 2 is adjacent to at least one leaf. This is false. A simple counterexample is a path graph on 5 vertices (P_5). In P_5, the middle vertex has degree 2, but its two neighbors also have degree 2. Therefore, it is a vertex of degree at least 2 that is not adjacent to any leaf. Since the statement is false, a proof cannot be constructed.
counterexample: A path graph on 5 vertices (P_5), e.g., with edges {1,2}, {2,3}, {3,4}, {4,5}. Vertex 3 has degree 2, but its neighbors (vertices 2 and 4) both have degree 2, meaning vertex 3 is not adjacent to any leaf (degree 1 vertex).
